svg.title: Neocloud Utilization Thresholds
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-neocloud-utilization-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: Neocloud Utilization Thresholds; subtitle: Where an H100 fleet stops beating broad stocks; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Full utilization; value: 100; display: 100%; conversion: 28% CAGR on the modeled H100; detail: H100 bought for $25K plus $5K opex, rented at $2.30/hr for about 4 years.; label: Workload-aware scheduler; value: 85; display: ~85%; conversion: ~$150k per day ahead of default scheduling; detail: Modeled on a 10,000-GPU fleet costing about $400M across 1,250 hosts in 32 racks.; label: Break-even against broad stocks; value: 55; display: ~55%; conversion: At or below this, broad stocks win; detail: Same $25K H100 model at $2.30/hr.; label: Commitment gate at a 50% contract discount; value: 50; display: 50%; conversion: Sign only where utilization clears 1 minus the discount; detail: Neocloud contracts run up to 30 to 50% cheaper; the commitment rule applied to the top of that range.; label: Default Kubernetes scheduler; value: 45; display: ~45%; conversion: Below the break-even line; detail: Default scheduling on the same 10,000-GPU model fleet.; caption: Idle or stalled GPUs bleed money, so the scheduler decides which side of break-even a fleet lands on.; assumptions note: The 50% stage applies The Code Notebook's one-minus-discount rule to the TMLS 30 to 50% contract range; every other value is as reported.; note: Sources: Caleb Writes Code (9u2hCf8FlW0), Codemia (a_zou7QahAo), The Code Notebook (IZtzUfhm8LU), Toronto Machine Learning Society (_oWJ0t-RW7o).

rect.title: label: Full utilization; value: 100; display: 100%; conversion: 28% CAGR on the modeled H100; detail: H100 bought for $25K plus $5K opex, rented at $2.30/hr for about 4 years.

label: Workload-aware scheduler; value: 85; display: ~85%; conversion: ~$150k per day ahead of default scheduling; detail: Modeled on a 10,000-GPU fleet costing about $400M across 1,250 hosts in 32 racks.
label: Break-even against broad stocks; value: 55; display: ~55%; conversion: At or below this, broad stocks win; detail: Same $25K H100 model at $2.30/hr.

label: Commitment gate at a 50% contract discount; value: 50; display: 50%; conversion: Sign only where utilization clears 1 minus the discount; detail: Neocloud contracts run up to 30 to 50% cheaper; the commitment rule applied to the top of that range.

text.title: Commitment gate at a 50% contract discount: 50

rect.title: label: Default Kubernetes scheduler; value: 45; display: ~45%; conversion: Below the break-even line; detail: Default scheduling on the same 10,000-GPU model fleet.

text.title: Assumptions: The 50% stage applies The Code Notebook's one-minus-discount rule to the TMLS 30 to 50% contract range; every other value is as reported.
